before.title: The guided-ring Sagnac delay: return times and receiver proper-time difference for counter-propagating guided signals on a rotating ring
before.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance and post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions (x^0 = c t). Let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Fix R > 0, a real Omega with |Omega| R < c, a real x^3_0 and a real phi_0, and put gamma := (1 - Omega^2 R^2/c^2)^{-1/2}. A rigidly rotating circular ring of radius R and height x^3_0 about the x^3-axis, with angular velocity Omega, has material worldlines W_{phi_0}(t) := x^{-1}(c t, R cos(phi_0 + Omega t), R sin(phi_0 + Omega t), x^3_0), t in R. (i) The ring worldline and the ring congruence. W_{phi_0} is a C^infinity future timelike worldline with four-velocity gamma(R) (1, -(Omega R/c) sin(phi_0+Omega t), (Omega R/c) cos(phi_0+Omega t), 0) = (gamma/c) partial_t|_{varphi}, where varphi := phi - Omega t is the rotating angular label of the ring material points; it is a flow line of the rigid-rotation congruence n = gamma(r) [partial_0 + (Omega/c)(-x^2 partial_1 + x^1 partial_2)] restricted to r = R, and its proper time tau and the chart time t satisfy d tau = dt/gamma, so tau and t differ from each other by the constant factor gamma on this worldline (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c), def-sr-proper-time, lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (ii) The guided-signal model. Adopt, as an explicit model assumption of an ideal circular guide attached to the ring and of the signal and detector model below, and not as a consequence of the postulates: two ideal signals are emitted at the common emission event W_{phi_0}(0) into the guide, one co-rotating with the ring and one counter-rotating, and in the inertial chart they follow the curves C_+ and C_- given by phi_+(t) = phi_0 + c t/R and phi_-(t) = phi_0 - c t/R with radius R and height x^3_0, i.e. each guided signal has chart angular rate +c/R or -c/R along the guide ('inertial tangential speed c along the guide'); the detector is an ideal clock carried by the ring material point labelled varphi = phi_0. Each of C_+ and C_- is a future null curve of the chart: its tangent has time component c and spatial part of Euclidean length c, so the tangent has eta-norm 0 and positive time component (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). (iii) Return times and differences. C_+ meets the worldline W_{phi_0} exactly at the chart times 2 pi k R/(c - Omega R), k in Z, and C_- exactly at the chart times 2 pi k R/(c + Omega R), k in Z; the smallest positive meeting times are t_1 := 2 pi R/(c - Omega R) > 0 and t_2 := 2 pi R/(c + Omega R) > 0. Hence the two counter-propagating signals emitted at the same event reunite with the emitting material point at the reception events W_{phi_0}(t_1) and W_{phi_0}(t_2), each having gained exactly one circuit relative to that material point, and the chart-time difference of the two reunions is t_1 - t_2 = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2 R^2) > 0 for Omega > 0. The proper-time difference measured by the detector ideal clock is (t_1 - t_2)/gamma = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)). For Omega = 0 (inertial ring) t_1 = t_2 = 2 pi R/c and both differences vanish; for Omega < 0 the sign of the first difference reverses and the roles of C_+ and C_- are interchanged. (iv) Relation to the ring rest-synchronization holonomy. The rest lines of the ring congruence are the curves of constant rotating label satisfying dt/dvarphi = Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2); one circuit varphi -> varphi + 2 pi has the chart-time holonomy Delta t_h = 2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) = (t_1 - t_2)/2 and the receiver proper-time holonomy Delta tau_h = Delta t_h/gamma = 2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)) = (1/2)(t_1 - t_2)/gamma, exactly half of the detector proper-time difference of (iii); for Omega = 0 both holonomies vanish. The ambient three-dimensional rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable for Omega != 0, so no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists, while the one-dimensional rest distribution restricted to the cylinder r = R is locally integrable and has the nonvanishing global holonomy just computed; the return-time computation of (iii) uses only the guided null curves and the material worldline and does not use either integrability property (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c), thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius). (v) Scope. All quantities are conditional model computations for the specified ring, guide, signal and detector idealizations. The guided-signal curves are an adopted device model: the ideal vacuum light rays of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light are straight future null lines and do not circulate around the ring by themselves, and no assertion is made about optical fibers, refractive media, dispersion, absorption, finite resolution, apparatus calibration, interference phase or wave optics, or about one-way synchronization conventions between distinct ring observers; no measurement outcome, statistical inference or empirical claim is made, the values of R and Omega are parameters and not measured quantities, and no choice principle is used.

(ii) Each curve C_+-, t |-> x^{-1}(c t, R cos(phi_0 +- c t/R), R sin(phi_0 +- c t/R), x^3_0), has tangent (c, -+ c sin(phi_0 +- ct/R), +- c cos(phi_0 +- ct/R), 0) of eta-norm -c^2 + c^2 = 0 and positive time component, hence is future null (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). The special cases Omega = 0 and Omega < 0 are substitutions. (v) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

before.statement: Worked instance of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay. Let R > 0 and Omega = 3c/(5R), so that Omega R = 3c/5, |Omega|R < c and gamma = (1 - 9/25)^{-1/2} = 5/4. Work in the inertial chart with x^0 = c t and let the ring have its plane x^3 = 0 and let the emission event be E = x^{-1}(0, R, 0, 0), where the material point labelled varphi = 0 has phi_0 = 0. (a) Return times. The co-rotating guided signal has phi_+(t) = c t/R and the emitting material point has phi(t) = Omega t = 3c t/(5R); the signal meets that point when c t/R = 3c t/(5R) + 2 pi, i.e. t_1 = 5 pi R/c (the relative angular rate is 8c/(5R)); the counter-rotating signal C_-, phi_-(t) = -c t/R, meets it when -c t/R = 3c t/(5R) - 2 pi, i.e. t_2 = 5 pi R/(4c). The reception events are e_1 = x^{-1}(5 pi R, R cos(3 pi), R sin(3 pi), 0) = x^{-1}(5 pi R, -R, 0, 0) and e_2 = x^{-1}(5 pi R/4, R cos(3 pi/4), R sin(3 pi/4), 0) = x^{-1}(5 pi R/4, -R/sqrt(2), R/sqrt(2), 0), where the angle values use the parity, addition and Pythagorean identities for sine and cosine (def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero, thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas, cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity). (b) Differences and the factor-2 holonomy check. The chart-time difference of the two reunions is t_1 - t_2 = 5 pi R/c - 5 pi R/(4c) = 15 pi R/(4c) = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2), and the detector proper-time difference is (t_1-t_2)·(4/5) = 3 pi R/c = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)). The ring rest-line chart-time holonomy of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay (iv) is Delta t_h = 15 pi R/(8c), exactly half of t_1 - t_2, and the corresponding receiver proper-time holonomy is (4/5)·15 pi R/(8c) = 3 pi R/(2c), exactly half of 3 pi R/c; this verifies the factor-2 relation of that clause. The ambient rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable while the cylinder-restricted one-dimensional rest distribution is locally integrable with the nonzero global holonomy 15 pi R/(8c) (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c)). (c) Inertial limit. For Omega = 0 with the same R the two return times are both 2 pi R/c and both differences vanish. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with the adopted ideal circular guide, ideal signals and the ideal clock detector of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay (ii); no interference phase, apparatus, medium, measurement, statistical or empirical claim is made, and the idealizations of that theorem are retained.

The ambient rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable while the fixed-height-cylinder-restricted one-dimensional rest distribution is locally integrable with the nonzero global holonomy 15 pi R/(8c) (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c)). (c) Inertial limit. For Omega = 0 with the same R the two return times are both 2 pi R/c and both differences vanish. (d) Scope. Conditional model computation with the adopted ideal circular guide, ideal signals and the ideal clock detector of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay (ii); no interference phase, apparatus, medium, measurement, statistical or empirical claim is made, and the idealizations of that theorem are retained.
after.strategy: Substitute Omega = 3c/(5R) into the exact formulas of pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay. (a) The angle of the material point is phi(t) = Omega t = 3c t/(5R); the co-rotating guided signal has angle c t/R, so the relative angular rate is 2c/(5R) and the reunion condition is c t/R = 3c t/(5R) + 2 pi k, with smallest positive solution k = 1, i.e. t_1 = 2 pi R/(c - 3c/5) = 5 pi R/c; the counter-rotating signal has angle -c t/R, so the signed relative angular rate is -8c/(5R) and the condition is -c t/R = 3c t/(5R) - 2 pi k, i.e. t_2 = 2 pi R/(c + 3c/5) = 5 pi R/(4c). supplier_inspections.statement_read: $\sin\pi=0$, and $\sin x>0$ for every $x$ with $0<x<\pi$. Thus $\pi$ is the first positive zero of sine.

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\qquad\cos(-x)=\cos x,\qquad\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.$$
Consequently $|\sin x|\le1$ and $|\cos x|\le1$.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let (V,eta) be a Lorentz vector space. A vector v in V is timelike if eta(v,v) < 0, null (or lightlike) if v is nonzero and eta(v,v) = 0, spacelike if eta(v,v) > 0, and causal if it is timelike or null. The zero vector is none of timelike, null or spacelike. The sign of eta(v,v) is the causal character of v. The pairing eta itself is written <v,w> := eta(v,w) when no confusion arises. Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.
supplier_inspections.strategy: The classification is by the sign of the real number eta(v,v); the three alternatives eta(v,v) < 0, eta(v,v) = 0, eta(v,v) > 0 for v nonzero are mutually exclusive and exhaustive by trichotomy of the order on R, and the zero vector is excluded from the null case by definition.

supplier_inspections.statement_read:
Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]), neighbourhoods are those of
[[def-neighbourhood-r]] and limit points those of [[def-limit-point-r]].

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $c \in A$ be a
**limit point of $A$**. The **difference quotient of $f$ at $c$** is the function

$$q_{f,c} : A \setminus \{c\} \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad q_{f,c}(x) := \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

The division is legitimate at every point of the domain, since $x \ne c$ gives
$x - c \ne 0$.

**The point $c$ is a limit point of $A \setminus \{c\}$, not merely of $A$.**
For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the punctured neighbourhood
$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c)$ omits $c$, so

$$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap A \;=\; N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap (A \setminus \{c\}) ,$$

and the left-hand side is nonempty because $c$ is a limit point of $A$. So
$q_{f,c}$ is a function on a set having $c$ as a limit point, and
$\lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x)$ is a notion that [[def-function-limit]] defines.

$f$ is **differentiable at $c$** when that limit exists, and then the
**derivative of $f$ at $c$** is

$$f'(c) \;:=\; \lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x) \;=\; \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

**Two obligations are carried by that notation, and both are discharged here.**

1. **Uniqueness.** Writing $f'(c)$ treats the right-hand side as a name for a
   single real number. That is legitimate: $c$ is a limit point of the domain
   $A \setminus \{c\}$ of $q_{f,c}$, so at most one real can satisfy the
   $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, by [[lem-function-limit-unique]] applied to
   $q_{f,c}$. Two reals both meeting the condition are therefore equal, and the
   symbol denotes.
2. **Meaningfulness.** The hypothesis that $c$ is a limit point of $A$ is not
   decoration. At an **isolated** point of $A$ the punctured condition
   $0 < |x - c| < \delta$ is met by no point of the domain at all, so the
   $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ formula is satisfied vacuously by *every* real at
   once; this is why [[def-function-limit]] leaves the limit undefined there,
   and it is why this library defines $f'(c)$ only at a limit point of $A$. At
   an isolated point of its domain a function is neither differentiable nor
   non-differentiable here: the question is not posed.

**The limit sees only $A \setminus \{c\}$, so how the difference quotient is
extended to $c$ is irrelevant.** Let $Q : A \to \mathbb{R}$ agree with
$q_{f,c}$ at every point of $A \setminus \{c\}$, and let $L \in \mathbb{R}$.
Then $\lim_{x \to c} Q(x) = L$ if and only if $\lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x) = L$.
Both conditions read: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real
$\delta > 0$ such that every point $x$ of the relevant domain with
$0 < |x - c| < \delta$ satisfies $|{\cdot} - L| < \varepsilon$
([[def-function-limit]]). The clause $0 < |x - c|$ removes $x = c$ from both
quantifiers, so in both cases the points quantified over are exactly the
$x \in A \setminus \{c\}$ with $0 < |x - c| < \delta$, at which $Q$ and
$q_{f,c}$ take the same value. The two conditions are the same condition.

**Differentiability on a set.** For $S \subseteq A$, $f$ is **differentiable on
$S$** when it is differentiable at every $c \in S$; implicit in that phrase is
that every point of $S$ is a limit point of $A$. $f$ is **differentiable** when
it is differentiable on the whole of $A$.

**Restriction of the domain.** Let $B \subseteq A$, let $c \in B$ and suppose
$c$ is a limit point of $B$. If $f$ is differentiable at $c$, then so is the
restriction $f|_B : B \to \mathbb{R}$, and

$$(f|_B)'(c) \;=\; f'(c) .$$

Indeed $B \setminus \{c\} \subseteq A \setminus \{c\}$; the displayed identity
of punctured neighbourhoods above, applied to $B$, shows that $c$ is a limit
point of $B \setminus \{c\}$; the difference quotient $q_{f|_B, c}$ is the
restriction of $q_{f,c}$ to $B \setminus \{c\}$, since $f|_B(c) = f(c)$; and
claim 2 of [[lem-limit-is-local]] carries the limit to that restriction.

**Every point of a nondegenerate interval is a limit point of it.** Let
$J \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex ([[def-interval]]) with at least two
elements and let $p \in J$. Choose $q \in J$ with $q \ne p$, and let a real
$\varepsilon > 0$ be given. If $p < q$, put $y := p + \tfrac{1}{2}\min\{\varepsilon,\ q - p\}$;
then $p < y$, and $y - p \le \tfrac{1}{2}(q-p) < q - p$, so $p < y < q$ and
order-convexity gives $y \in J$, while $0 < |y - p| < \varepsilon$. If $q < p$,
the point $y := p - \tfrac{1}{2}\min\{\varepsilon,\ p - q\}$ serves in the same
way. So $N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(p) \cap J \ne \varnothing$ for every real
$\varepsilon > 0$, that is, $p$ is a limit point of $J$
([[def-limit-point-r]]).

Consequently, for $f$ defined on a nondegenerate interval $I$, the symbol
$f'(c)$ is meaningful at **every** $c \in I$, endpoints included. At an endpoint
the difference quotient is taken over the points of $I$ lying on the one side
that is available, so what other texts call a one-sided derivative is, here,
simply the derivative of $f$ on $I$.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. An inertial frame of the model is a tuple (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) consisting of an event o in A and an ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of V that is eta-orthonormal (eta(e_a,e_b) = diag(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}), future (e_0 is in C^+) and positively oriented (the ordered basis class of (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is the fixed orientation of V). Its inertial chart is the map x: A -> R^4, x(p) := E^{-1}(p-o), where E: R^4 -> V is the linear isomorphism E(u) := sum_a u^a e_a; its components x^a(p) are the inertial coordinates of the event p, and x(p) = 0 exactly at p = o. The family of all inertial frames and charts is the inertial atlas of the model; two inertial charts x, x' are related by x' = M^{-1}(x - x(o')) for M the change-of-basis matrix between the two ordered bases, so transitions are affine bijections of R^4.
supplier_inspections.strategy: Well-definedness requires the existence of eta-orthonormal bases (orthonormal-basis lemma) and the possibility of making them future and positively oriented (existence lemma below). The transition formula follows from the definitions: if e'_a = sum_b M^b_a e_b, then for p = o + sum_a x^a e_a one has p = o' + sum_a x'^a e'_a with x' = M^{-1}(x - x(o')), because applying E'^{-1} to the displacement identity p - o' = (p-o) + (o-o') gives exactly that expression; that x' = 0 iff p = o' is then immediate.

supplier_inspections.statement_read:
Let $\gamma$ be the unique smallest positive zero of cosine supplied by [[thm-cosine-has-a-smallest-positive-zero]]. Define
$$\pi:=2\gamma.$$

Thus $\pi>0$ and $\pi/2=\gamma$.

supplier_inspections.statement: An oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space is a quadruple (A,V,eta,C^+) consisting of: a nonempty affine space A over a 4-dimensional real vector space V (def-affine-space-and-displacement); a Lorentz form eta on V (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia); an orientation of V, i.e. a positive ray of the determinant line Lambda^4 V, fixed once and for all (def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space); and a time orientation C^+ of (V,eta) (def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). The points of A are called events; q-p is the displacement from p to q; the interval of p,q in A is I(p,q) := eta(q-p,q-p); and p,q are timelike, null, spacelike or causally related when q-p is timelike, null, spacelike or causal, future-related when q-p is future causal, and past-related when q-p is past causal (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). No point of A is distinguished: for every v in V the translation p |-> p+v is a bijection of A preserving all the structure except the labelling of points. All later structure of this framework (frames, charts, tensor fields, worldlines) is built on this model, and no derived physical quantity is part of it.
supplier_inspections.strategy: The definition is a structure specification: the affine action, the form, the orientation and the time orientation are separately defined objects, and the definition only bundles them and fixes the terminology (events, displacement, interval, causal relations). Well-definedness of the bundled data requires the existence and uniqueness statements supplied by the cited items: affine coordinates are available by the affine-space definition, the orthonormal basis needed later exists by the orthonormal-basis lemma, and the two components of the timelike set needed to choose C^+ exist by the components lemma. The translation invariance claim follows from the affine axioms: displacements are unchanged by translations, and translations have identity linear part, so they preserve eta, the orientation and C^+.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with proper-time function tau and inverse rho: J -> I (def-sr-proper-time, lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (a) The four-velocity of x is the map U: I -> V defined by U(s) := x'(s)/tau'(s) = c x'(s)/sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))); equivalently U(s) is the tangent at parameter value s of the proper-time parametrized worldline x o rho, read at the proper-time parameter tau(s). U is continuous, U(s) is future timelike for every s, and U does not depend on the base point chosen for tau. (b) If x is C^2, that is, x' is differentiable with continuous derivative, the four-acceleration of x is the map A: I -> V defined by A(s) := U'(s)/tau'(s) = c U'(s)/sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))); equivalently A is the derivative of the four-velocity with respect to the proper-time parameter along the worldline. A is continuous. (c) The dimensionless four-velocity of x is u := U/c. A point observer of the model at an event is a future unit timelike vector n in V, eta(n,n) = -1; the four-velocity of the observer's own worldline is cn at each of its events. (d) The names four-velocity and four-acceleration are the model's names for U and A; the physical interpretation, including the units in which U and A are measured, is supplied with the model's coordinate conventions and is not part of the affine geometry. The definition makes no claim that U has norm -c^2 or that A is orthogonal to U; those are proved in thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition.
supplier_inspections.strategy: Definition item: it introduces the two derived vector fields along a worldline and fixes their well-definedness. Obligations: (i) the division by tau'(s) is legitimate because tau' > 0 by lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization; (ii) the identification U(s) = (x o rho)'(tau(s)) is the chain rule applied componentwise in an inertial chart (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, thm-chain-rule), and it shows that U is the tangent field of the proper-time parametrized worldline; (iii) continuity of U follows from continuity of x' and tau' and continuity of division by the positive function tau'; (iv) A is defined only when x is C^2, in which case U' exists; (v) neither the norm of U nor the orthogonality of A with U is asserted here, so the definition cannot be used as if those identities were definitional. No choice principle is used.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let n be an observer congruence on a nonempty open subset Omega of A (def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction), let nabla be the flat covariant derivative (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space), and write n_b := eta_{bc} n^c for the associated covector field. (a) Rest metric and projection. Define h(v,w) := eta(v,w) + eta(n,v) eta(n,w) for vectors at the same point, so h = eta + n-flat (x) n-flat; then h(v,w) = eta(h(v),h(w)) where h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n is the orthogonal projection of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c). At every point h is symmetric with radical spanned by n(p), and its restriction to n(p)^perp is positive definite. (b) Acceleration. The acceleration of the congruence is a := nabla_n n; then eta(n,a) = 0 pointwise, because 2 eta(n, nabla_n n) = n(eta(n,n)) = 0, so a(p) is spacelike or zero by the causal classification. In the model's physical interpretation the four-acceleration of the congruence observers is c^2 a and its magnitude is c^2 sqrt(eta(a,a)); the numerical units belong to the model's SI conventions and are not part of the affine geometry. (c) Kinematic decomposition. Set theta_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{(c} n_{d)} and omega_{ab} := h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{[c} n_{d]}, where nabla_{(c} n_{d)} = (1/2)(nabla_c n_d + nabla_d n_c) and nabla_{[c} n_{d]} = (1/2)(nabla_c n_d - nabla_d n_c). Then nabla_a n_b = -n_a a_b + theta_{ab} + omega_{ab}, with theta symmetric, omega antisymmetric, both horizontal (theta_{ab} n^b = omega_{ab} n^b = n^a theta_{ab} = n^a omega_{ab} = 0), and this decomposition is unique with these properties. theta is the expansion (and shear) tensor, theta := h^{ab} theta_{ab} is the expansion scalar, its trace-free part is the shear, and omega is the vorticity 2-tensor. (d) Born rigidity. The congruence is Born rigid (describes a rigid motion) if L_n h = 0. Since (L_n h)_{ab} = 2 theta_{ab}, Born rigidity is equivalent to theta = 0, equivalently to the projected symmetrized derivative of n-flat vanishing. (e) Scope. These are kinematic definitions for a prescribed smooth field n on the affine model; no dynamical equation, matter model, global synchronization or completeness is assumed, and a, theta, omega and h are local objects on Omega.
supplier_inspections.strategy: Definition item with content clauses proved by finite algebra. (i) h(v,w) = eta(h(v),h(w)) is expansion using eta(n,n) = -1; the radical and positive definiteness of the restriction to n^perp are clause (c) of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition. (ii) eta(n,a) = 0 is the derivative of eta(n,n) = -1 along n, computed with metric compatibility; a is therefore spacelike or zero by the causal classification. (iii) The decomposition follows by splitting nabla_a n_b into its component along n and its horizontal part: n^a nabla_a n_b = a_b, the mixed terms are n_a a_b, the horizontal part splits uniquely into its symmetric and antisymmetric parts, and the stated contractions vanish because n is unit. (iv) L_n eta = nabla_a n_b + nabla_b n_a in a torsion-free metric-compatible connection; L_n(n-flat) = a-flat because L_n n_b = n^a nabla_a n_b + n_a nabla_b n^a = a_b and n_a nabla_b n^a = (1/2) nabla_b(eta(n,n)) = 0; substituting the decomposition gives (L_n h)_{ab} = 2 theta_{ab}, so Born rigidity is theta = 0. (v) All computations are pointwise finite algebra in the four-dimensional vector space, with no coordinate condition and no choice principle.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let c > 0 be a fixed real number (the conversion constant of the model, whose physical interpretation is supplied with the model's coordinate conventions) and let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline). Then the function g_x: I -> R, g_x(s) := -eta(x'(s),x'(s)), is continuous and strictly positive: continuity holds because in an eta-orthonormal basis eta(x'(s),x'(s)) = sum_{a,b} eta_ab (x'(s))^a (x'(s))^b is a finite sum of products of continuous real functions (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis, thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions), and positivity is the future timelike hypothesis (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors). Hence u |-> sqrt(g_x(u)) is continuous on I (thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives, thm-composition-of-continuous-functions) and Riemann integrable on every compact subinterval of I (thm-continuous-implies-integrable). For s_0, s in I the proper time from s_0 to s is tau(s) := c^{-1} integral_{s_0}^{s} sqrt(-eta(x'(u),x'(u))) du, the integral being the oriented integral of def-oriented-integral; explicitly, for a < b in I, tau(b) - tau(a) = c^{-1} integral_a^b sqrt(-eta(x'(u),x'(u))) du, and changing the base point s_0 changes tau by an additive constant. tau depends on the parametrized history of x and on the parameter values; its invariance under increasing C^1 reparametrizations is proved in lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. For the straight future timelike segment x(s) = p + (s - s_0)(q - p) one has tau(b) - tau(a) = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) (b - a), which is the straight-segment proper time of the model's coordinate conventions. The construction is restricted to future timelike worldlines: at a null point the integrand vanishes, for a spacelike curve -eta(x',x') is negative and the square root is not a real number, and for a past-directed timelike curve the integral is defined but is not attached to a worldline of the model.
supplier_inspections.strategy: Definition item with well-definedness obligations: (i) the integrand is the composition of the continuous map s |-> x'(s), the continuous quadratic form v |-> -eta(v,v) (checked in coordinates in an eta-orthonormal basis, since eta is bilinear on the finite-dimensional V) and the continuous power t |-> t^{1/2} on (0,inf); (ii) strict positivity of g_x is exactly the future timelike hypothesis, so the square root is a positive real number on all of I; (iii) existence of the integral on compact subintervals is thm-continuous-implies-integrable, and the oriented convention makes tau(s_0) = 0 and reverses the sign when the endpoints are exchanged; (iv) the base point enters only additively, so elapsed times between parameter values are intrinsic; (v) the straight-segment consistency is a direct evaluation: x' is constant on a straight segment and the integrand is c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) times the parameter length. No choice principle is used. The item deliberately does not assert that tau is differentiable or invertible (that is lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization) nor that a physical clock reads tau (that belongs to the adopted physical interpretation).

supplier_inspections.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model) and let I be an order-convex subset of R with at least two elements (def-interval); a curve of the model is a map x: I -> A. (a) Derivative and regularity of the parametrization. For s in I and h nonzero with s + h in I the difference quotient (x(s+h) - x(s))/h is an element of V, the displacement from x(s) to x(s+h) divided by the real number h; the curve is differentiable at s when the limit of these quotients as h -> 0 exists in the finite-dimensional real vector space V, and then this limit, written x'(s) in V, is the tangent vector of x at s. If x_A: A -> R^4 is the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), then x is differentiable at s exactly when the R^4-valued map x_A o x is differentiable at s in the sense of def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, and then x'(s) = E((x_A o x)'(s)), where E: R^4 -> V is the frame isomorphism; this does not depend on the inertial chart used, because inertial chart transitions are affine, hence smooth (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas), and all norms on the finite-dimensional V give the same limit. The curve is C^1 when it is differentiable at every point of I and the derivative map s |-> x'(s), I -> V, is continuous (def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity); it is C^k for k >= 1 when x' is C^{k-1}. A curve on a compact interval [a,b] contained in I is piecewise C^1 when there is a finite partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b such that x is C^1 on every open subinterval (s_{i-1},s_i) and the finite one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both ends of every piece exist in V. These are limits of (x(t+h)-x(t))/h over the relevant side of the piece, not assertions that x'(s) has a limit as s approaches a corner. Their finiteness implies continuity of x at the corners. No continuous extension of the open-piece derivative is required. Derivatives at the endpoints of I are the one-sided difference-quotient limits over I. (b) Causal character. Let x be differentiable at s in I. Then x is regular at s if x'(s) is not the zero vector; x is timelike (respectively null, spacelike, causal) at s if the vector x'(s) is timelike (respectively null, spacelike, causal) in the sense of def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, and x is future-directed at s if x'(s) is future timelike or future null in the sense of def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets. The zero vector has no causal character, so only a regular curve has a causal character at s. (c) Worldlines. A future timelike worldline (massive worldline) is a C^1 curve x: I -> A with x'(s) future timelike for every s in I; a future causal curve (respectively a future null curve) is a C^1 curve with x'(s) future causal (respectively future null) for every s in I. A piecewise C^1 worldline is a piecewise C^1 curve whose tangents at every point of each open smooth piece and whose finite one-sided difference-quotient tangents at both endpoints of every piece are future timelike, and a C^k worldline is a worldline whose parametrization is C^k; C^2 regularity is what makes the four-acceleration of this page available. The parametrization is part of the curve: the image of a future timelike worldline is also the image of the past-directed curve s |-> x(-s), which is not a worldline of this model, and no worldline or clock claim is attached to it. The definition asserts the existence of no worldline beyond those given by an explicit formula.
supplier_inspections.strategy: A definition item: it fixes the curve, regularity and causal-character language on which the page's items rest, and makes no proof claim beyond well-definedness. Obligations: (i) the difference quotient is an element of V because the affine action gives a displacement for every ordered pair of events, and the limit is taken in the finite-dimensional real vector space V, so no norm has to be chosen; (ii) the identification with the coordinate calculus and the independence of x'(s) and of C^k from the inertial chart are justified by the affine, hence smooth, chart transitions of lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas, with the published vector-valued derivative of def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral as the coordinate calculus; (iii) continuity of x' is continuity of a V-valued map (def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity), and one-sided derivatives at endpoints are limits over the domain I as in def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral; (iv) causal character and the future/past alternative are those of the model's vector classification and time orientation, with the zero vector excluded, so regularity is implicit in every causal character; (v) null and spacelike curves are distinguished from massive worldlines and are used later only to delimit the proper-time construction. No choice principle is used: all objects are finite-dimensional or explicitly parametrized. In the piecewise clause, a finite one-sided quotient derivative v gives x(t+h)-x(t)=h(v+o(1)), proving one-sided endpoint continuity directly. It does not imply convergence of the interior derivative; no such hypothesis is added. The timelike condition applies at every smooth point and to each side of a corner, and excludes zero tangents.

supplier_inspections.statement: This framework fixes the following SI coordinate and unit conventions. In every inertial chart the coordinates are x^0 = c t, x^1, x^2, x^3, where c > 0 is the adopted conversion constant in metres per second and the spatial coordinates are measured in metres along the frame's orthonormal spatial directions; all four x^a carry the unit metre, the matrix of eta in an inertial chart is diag(-1,1,1,1) with dimensionless entries, and the interval I(p,q) carries the unit m^2. For a timelike displacement the number tau := c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) has the unit second and is the proper time of the straight timelike segment from p to q. A timelike worldline's four-velocity U = dx/dtau has unit m/s, four-acceleration m/s^2, four-momentum kg m/s, and observer energy joule. If instead a chart uses a temporal coordinate t in seconds, then the corresponding metric component is g_tt = -c^2 with unit m^2/s^2 and the mixed time-space components acquire the unit m/s; formulas derived in one convention are not reused unchanged in the other. Natural units (c = 1) may be used only together with an explicit restoration table for c. The numerical value of c is an empirical parameter of the model; SI unit status does not make a quantity primitive in this theory.
supplier_inspections.strategy: A convention definition: it fixes the coordinate normalization (x^0 = ct rather than t), the unit of each component, and the dimensional interpretation of the interval, of proper time along a timelike straight segment and of the derived kinematic quantities, all relative to the adopted model and its inertial charts. The dimensional statements follow by inspection of the inertial coordinate expressions out of the diagonal form of eta, and the warning about the temporal-coordinate convention records where the components change dimension.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let (V,eta) be a Lorentz vector space and let T := {v in V : eta(v,v) < 0} be its timelike set. By the components lemma T has exactly two connected components; a time orientation of (V,eta) is a choice of one of them. Fixing such a choice and writing C^+ for the chosen component and C^- := T \ C^+ for the other, call v future timelike if v is in C^+, past timelike if v is in C^-, future null if v is nonzero, eta(v,v) = 0 and v lies in the closure cl(C^+), past null if v is nonzero, eta(v,v) = 0 and v lies in cl(C^-), future causal if it is future timelike or future null, and past causal if it is past timelike or past null. The sets cl(C^+) and cl(C^-) are the future and past closed cones; they are convex cones meeting only at 0, and a causal vector is future or past but not both.
supplier_inspections.strategy: Well-definedness rests on the components lemma: T has exactly two components, so 'a choice of one of them' names a definite pair {C^+,C^-}. The claimed properties of the closures (convexity, the intersection {0}, and exclusivity of the future and past causal sets) are proved in the components lemma via the orthonormal coordinate description {v^0 >= |v_vec|} and {v^0 <= -|v_vec|} of the two closed cones.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with proper-time function tau, tau(s) = c^{-1} integral_{s_0}^{s} sqrt(-eta(x'(u),x'(u))) du (def-sr-proper-time). Then: (i) tau is differentiable at every s in I, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints of I, and tau'(s) = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))) > 0 for every s in I; since tau' is this composition of continuous maps, tau is C^1 on I. (ii) tau is strictly increasing on I, hence injective, and its image J := tau[I] is an order-convex subset of R with at least two elements, so tau: I -> J is a bijection. (iii) The inverse rho: J -> I of tau is continuous and strictly increasing, and it is differentiable at every point tau(s) of J with rho'(tau(s)) = 1/tau'(s) = c / sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))) > 0; hence rho is C^1 on J. (iv) The reparametrized curve y := x o rho: J -> A is a C^1 future timelike worldline whose tangent at the proper-time parameter tau(s) is (x o rho)'(tau(s)) = x'(s)/tau'(s) = c x'(s)/sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))); in particular y is parametrized by its own proper time up to the additive constant of the base point, and the derivative formula is the four-velocity of the following definition.
supplier_inspections.strategy: (i) thm-ftc-first-part applied to the continuous integrand u |-> c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x'(u),x'(u))) on a compact neighbourhood of s (contained in I using def-interval) gives tau'(s) equal to that value, with the one-sided reading at endpoints; positivity is the future timelike hypothesis. (ii) For a < b in I, monotonicity of the integral (thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral) gives tau(b) - tau(a) >= 0, and equality would force the continuous nonnegative integrand to vanish on [a,b] (thm-nonnegative-continuous-with-zero-integral-vanishes), contradicting its strict positivity; so tau is strictly increasing and injective, and its image is order-convex and nondegenerate by cor-continuous-image-of-an-interval-is-an-interval (tau is continuous). (iii) A continuous injective map on an interval has a continuous strictly monotone inverse (thm-continuous-inverse), and the reciprocal derivative formula is thm-derivative-of-an-inverse, applicable since tau'(s) > 0; tau' continuous gives rho C^1. (iv) Differentiating componentwise in an inertial chart and applying the one-variable chain rule to each coordinate (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, thm-chain-rule) gives (x o rho)' = (x' o rho) rho' at interior points, with one-sided readings at endpoints; rho' > 0 preserves future timelikeness. The base point shifts rho's argument and leaves derivatives unchanged. No choice principle is used.

supplier_inspections.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework: (i) Ideal clocks. Along a curve x: I -> A whose coordinate representation in an inertial chart is C^1 with everywhere future timelike derivative, an ideal clock carried along the curve reads, between parameters a < b in I, the elapsed time sigma(b) - sigma(a) = c^{-1} integral_a^b sqrt(-eta(x'(s),x'(s))) ds; there is no additional acceleration-dependent term in the reading (clock hypothesis). (ii) Ideal light. In vacuum, ideal light rays are exactly the future null straight lines {p + lambda v : lambda in R} with p in A and v a future null vector; in every inertial chart x^a such a ray has x(lambda) = x(p) + lambda (v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3) and coordinate speed c, so the adopted conversion constant c is the same in all inertial charts. Scope: ideal apparatus, complete vacuum, and the geometric (nondispersive) ray regime. The assumptions are adopted, not experimentally proved; no dispersive medium is described; no quantum photon model is assumed and in particular frequency is not identified with energy by a factor hbar; and real clocks and light are not claimed to be exactly ideal.
supplier_inspections.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it fixes the physical interpretation of the mathematical objects (future timelike curves, future null straight lines) and the reading rule of an ideal clock, together with the exact scope of the idealization. The integral is well defined because the integrand -eta(x',x') is positive and continuous on a compact parameter interval for a future timelike C^1 curve; parametrization invariance and the resulting proper-time parametrization, as well as the general theory of worldlines, four-velocity and acceleration, are developed on the later worldlines-and-clocks page, which may not depend on this page by a forward edge; the postulate therefore states the reading rule for the model rather than a theorem about curves.

supplier_inspections.statement: Adopt as a physical assumption of this framework: (i) the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) is the spacetime of the framework; its points represent idealized physical events, displacements represent idealized spacetime separations, and the sign classification of eta is the adopted causal structure; (ii) the equations of the specific mechanical and electromagnetic models developed from this framework are covariant under the affine maps F: A -> A whose linear part L satisfies eta(Lv,Lw) = eta(v,w) for all v,w in V, has determinant +1 relative to the adopted orientation, and maps C^+ onto C^+; such maps are the inertial changes of description. These assumptions are adopted, not deduced from experiment nor from the verbal postulates of Einstein, and they define the framework's scope. Covariance is asserted for the specified model equations only: it does not select a force or matter law, does not forbid explicitly adopted background structure by a purely syntactic test, and carries no claim that the physical world is exactly described by the model.
supplier_inspections.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: the item records the adopted formulation (affine Minkowski geometry with a fixed orientation and future cone) and the adopted covariance of the framework's model equations under future- and orientation-preserving eta-isometries of V. The maps are characterized by their defining properties rather than by a named group; the group structure, factorization and algebra of these maps are established on the Lorentz-transformations page. The exposition must state the scope limitation that covariance is a property of the specified model equations and neither proves the model nor selects dynamics.

supplier_inspections.statement: Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance and post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions (x^0 = c t). Let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Fix R > 0, a real Omega with |Omega| R < c, a real x^3_0 and a real phi_0, and put gamma := (1 - Omega^2 R^2/c^2)^{-1/2}. A rigidly rotating circular ring of radius R and height x^3_0 about the x^3-axis, with angular velocity Omega, has material worldlines W_{phi_0}(t) := x^{-1}(c t, R cos(phi_0 + Omega t), R sin(phi_0 + Omega t), x^3_0), t in R. (i) The ring worldline and the ring congruence. W_{phi_0} is a C^infinity future timelike worldline with four-velocity gamma(R) (1, -(Omega R/c) sin(phi_0+Omega t), (Omega R/c) cos(phi_0+Omega t), 0) = (gamma/c) partial_t|_{varphi}, where varphi := phi - Omega t is the rotating angular label of the ring material points; it is a flow line of the rigid-rotation congruence n = gamma(r) [partial_0 + (Omega/c)(-x^2 partial_1 + x^1 partial_2)] restricted to r = R, and its proper time tau and the chart time t satisfy d tau = dt/gamma, so tau and t differ from each other by the constant factor gamma on this worldline (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c), def-sr-proper-time, lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). (ii) The guided-signal model. Adopt, as an explicit model assumption of an ideal circular guide attached to the ring and of the signal and detector model below, and not as a consequence of the postulates: two ideal signals are emitted at the common emission event W_{phi_0}(0) into the guide, one co-rotating with the ring and one counter-rotating, and in the inertial chart they follow the curves C_+ and C_- given by phi_+(t) = phi_0 + c t/R and phi_-(t) = phi_0 - c t/R with radius R and height x^3_0, i.e. each guided signal has chart angular rate +c/R or -c/R along the guide ('inertial tangential speed c along the guide'); the detector is an ideal clock carried by the ring material point labelled varphi = phi_0. Each of C_+ and C_- is a future null curve of the chart: its tangent has time component c and spatial part of Euclidean length c, so the tangent has eta-norm 0 and positive time component (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). (iii) Return times and differences. C_+ meets the worldline W_{phi_0} exactly at the chart times 2 pi k R/(c - Omega R), k in Z, and C_- exactly at the chart times 2 pi k R/(c + Omega R), k in Z; the smallest positive meeting times are t_1 := 2 pi R/(c - Omega R) > 0 and t_2 := 2 pi R/(c + Omega R) > 0. Hence the two counter-propagating signals emitted at the same event reunite with the emitting material point at the reception events W_{phi_0}(t_1) and W_{phi_0}(t_2), each having gained exactly one circuit relative to that material point, and the chart-time difference of the two reunions is t_1 - t_2 = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2 R^2) > 0 for Omega > 0. The proper-time difference measured by the detector ideal clock is (t_1 - t_2)/gamma = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)). For Omega = 0 (inertial ring) t_1 = t_2 = 2 pi R/c and both differences vanish; for Omega < 0 the sign of the first difference reverses and the roles of C_+ and C_- are interchanged. (iv) Relation to the ring rest-synchronization holonomy. The rest lines of the ring congruence are the curves of constant rotating label satisfying dt/dvarphi = Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2); one circuit varphi -> varphi + 2 pi has the chart-time holonomy Delta t_h = 2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) = (t_1 - t_2)/2 and the receiver proper-time holonomy Delta tau_h = Delta t_h/gamma = 2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 sqrt(1 - Omega^2R^2/c^2)) = (1/2)(t_1 - t_2)/gamma, exactly half of the detector proper-time difference of (iii); for Omega = 0 both holonomies vanish. The ambient three-dimensional rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable for Omega != 0, so no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists, while the one-dimensional rest distribution restricted to the cylinder r = R is locally integrable and has the nonvanishing global holonomy just computed; the return-time computation of (iii) uses only the guided null curves and the material worldline and does not use either integrability property (thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c), thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius). (v) Scope. All quantities are conditional model computations for the specified ring, guide, signal and detector idealizations. The guided-signal curves are an adopted device model: the ideal vacuum light rays of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light are straight future null lines and do not circulate around the ring by themselves, and no assertion is made about optical fibers, refractive media, dispersion, absorption, finite resolution, apparatus calibration, interference phase or wave optics, or about one-way synchronization conventions between distinct ring observers; no measurement outcome, statistical inference or empirical claim is made, the values of R and Omega are parameters and not measured quantities, and no choice principle is used.
supplier_inspections.strategy: Direct computation on the cylinder r = R, using the ring congruence data of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c). (i) Substituting phi = phi_0 + Omega t into the cylinder parametrisation and differentiating with thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives, thm-chain-rule and def-derivative gives the displayed tangent; its eta-norm is gamma^2(-1 + Omega^2R^2/c^2) = -1, so it is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets), and the four-velocity relation to the congruence field n and the proper-time factor d tau = dt/gamma follow from dx/dtau = c n and def-sr-proper-time with lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization. (ii) Each curve C_+-, t |-> x^{-1}(c t, R cos(phi_0 +- c t/R), R sin(phi_0 +- c t/R), x^3_0), has tangent (c, -+ c sin(phi_0 +- ct/R), +- c cos(phi_0 +- ct/R), 0) of eta-norm -c^2 + c^2 = 0 and positive time component, hence is future null (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). (iii) C_+ meets W_{phi_0} exactly when c t/R = Omega t + 2 pi k for an integer k, i.e. t = 2 pi k R/(c - Omega R); since |Omega|R < c the denominator is positive, so the positive solutions are k = 1,2,..., the smallest being t_1 = 2 pi R/(c - Omega R) > 0. Likewise C_- meets W_{phi_0} exactly when -c t/R = Omega t + 2 pi k, i.e. t = 2 pi k R/(c + Omega R) for integer k, with smallest positive solution t_2 = 2 pi R/(c + Omega R). The difference is t_1 - t_2 = 2 pi R[(c + Omega R) - (c - Omega R)]/((c - Omega R)(c + Omega R)) = 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2), and multiplication by the constant factor 1/gamma of (i) converts chart time to detector proper time (lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization). The special cases Omega = 0 and Omega < 0 are substitutions. (iv) The rest lines and the holonomy are those computed in thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (c); the factor-2 relation is the algebraic identity 4 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2) = 2 (2 pi Omega R^2/(c^2 - Omega^2R^2)) and its proper-time counterpart, and the distinction between the nonintegrable ambient rest distribution and the locally integrable cylinder restriction is the statement of that theorem and of thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius (iii). (v) Scope only. No choice principle is used.

supplier_inspections.statement_read:
Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

**Both limit-point hypotheses are needed, and neither is automatic.** That $c$
is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(x+\pi/2)=\cos x,\quad\cos(x+\pi/2)=-\sin x,\quad\sin(x+\pi)=-\sin x,\quad\cos(x+\pi)=-\cos x.$$
In particular,
$$\sin(\pi/2)=1,\quad\cos(\pi/2)=0,\quad\sin\pi=0,\quad\cos\pi=-1.$$

For all real $x,y$,
$$\sin(x+y)=\sin x\cos y+\cos x\sin y,$$
$$\cos(x+y)=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y.$$

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

For every real $x$,
$$\sin x=0\Longleftrightarrow x=m\pi\text{ for some }m\in\mathbb Z,\qquad \cos x=0\Longleftrightarrow x=(m+1/2)\pi\text{ for some }m\in\mathbb Z.$$
Both sine and cosine have period $2\pi$, and no smaller positive number is a common period.

supplier_inspections.statement: (a) Preservation. Let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline and let X,Y: I -> V be C^1 Fermi-Walker transported fields along x (def-sr-fermi-walker-transport). Then tau |-> eta(X(tau),Y(tau)) is constant on I; in particular Fermi-Walker transport preserves norms and orthogonality, and the unique Fermi-Walker transported family with initial values a tetrad (E_0(tau_0),...,E_3(tau_0)) with E_0(tau_0) = U(tau_0)/c is an orthonormal tetrad (E_0(tau),...,E_3(tau)) at every tau with E_0(tau) = U(tau)/c (observer-adapted tetrad), by lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b) Rindler wedge congruence. In an inertial chart (x^0,x,y,z) consider Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2, with theta in R and rho>0. Then Phi is a smooth bijection onto the right wedge W := {(x^0,x) : x > |x^0|}, with smooth inverse rho = sqrt(x^2 - (x^0)^2), theta = (1/2) log((x + x^0)/(x - x^0)); the pullback of eta is g = -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2; the field n := rho^{-1} partial/partial theta is a future unit timelike field on W whose congruence is Born rigid and irrotational, with acceleration a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial/partial rho, hence eta(a,a) = rho^{-2}; its rest slices theta = const are hyperplanes orthogonal to n with induced metric d rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 independent of theta; and the frame (n, partial/partial rho, partial/partial y, partial/partial z) is a tetrad field which is not a coordinate frame, since [n, partial/partial rho] = +(1/rho) n is nonzero (def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields). (c) Rigid rotation, ambient nonintegrability and ring holonomy. Fix real Omega. In the inertial chart let U_Omega be the open timelike region r^2=(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2<c^2/Omega^2 when Omega!=0, and the whole chart when Omega=0. On this four-dimensional open set put K=partial_0+(Omega/c)(-x^2 partial_1+x^1 partial_2), gamma(r)=(1-Omega^2 r^2/c^2)^(-1/2), and n=gamma(r)K. This is a smooth future unit timelike Born-rigid congruence. If Omega!=0, its three-dimensional rest distribution in the ambient open set is nowhere integrable: its vorticity is nowhere zero and no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists locally. If Omega=0, n=partial_0 is inertial and irrotational, and the rest hypersurfaces are x^0=const. Now fix R>0 with |Omega|R<c and restrict to the timelike ring cylinder r=R, x^3=const, whose rotating angle is varphi=phi-Omega t modulo2pi, x^0=ct. The ring observer phi=phi_0+Omega t has n=gamma(R)(1,-(Omega R/c)sin phi,(Omega R/c)cos phi,0). The induced metric is -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2Omega R^2 dt dvarphi+R^2 dvarphi^2. The ambient rest covector restricted to the cylinder is proportional to -(c^2-Omega^2R^2)dt+Omega R^2 dvarphi, so the one-dimensional rest distribution on that cylinder is locally integrable and satisfies dt/dvarphi=Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). After one positive circuit in the rotating label, its lift starting at t=0 has signed time offset Delta t=2pi Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2). For Omega!=0 it returns to the same rotating label at a different time and does not close as a ring rest-simultaneity curve; there is no globally single-valued real rest-synchronization time on the entire cylinder with time-oriented nonzero differential annihilating these rest lines. This global ring holonomy is distinct from the ambient local Frobenius obstruction. For Omega=0 the offset is zero and ring rest lines are t=const. (d) Bell congruence. Let q: J -> R^3 be C^2 with q(t) = (q_1(t),0,0) and |q_1'(t)| < c, and consider the congruence of translated worldlines x_xi(t) = (c t, q(t) + xi) parametrized by xi in an open subset of R^3, with n = gamma(1, q_1'(t)/c, 0, 0), gamma = (1 - q_1'(t)^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and unit longitudinal rest vector s = gamma(q_1'(t)/c, 1, 0, 0). Then theta(s,s) = s^a s^b partial_a n_b = gamma^3 q_1'(t) q_1''(t)/c^3, which is nonzero exactly when q_1'(t) q_1''(t) is nonzero; hence the congruence is not Born rigid on any neighbourhood of a parameter value with q_1'(t) q_1''(t) nonzero, although for every fixed chart time t the separation between the members labelled xi_1 and xi_2 is the constant |xi_1 - xi_2|. A breaking or fracture conclusion about a material rod would additionally require an elasticity model and a failure criterion and is not a kinematic statement.
supplier_inspections.strategy: (a) For Fermi-Walker transported X,Y, d/dtau eta(X,Y) = eta(X',Y) + eta(X,Y') and substituting X' = c^{-2}(eta(A,X)U - eta(U,X)A) and the analogous expression for Y' gives c^{-2}[eta(A,X)eta(U,Y) - eta(U,X)eta(A,Y) + eta(A,Y)eta(U,X) - eta(U,Y)eta(A,X)] = 0. The initial-tetrad family therefore remains orthonormal, and E_0 = U/c is transported by def-sr-fermi-walker-transport (b); uniqueness is lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness. (b) Injectivity of Phi follows from x^2 - (x^0)^2 = rho^2 and the sign of x; the inverse formulas are the standard hyperbolic identities cosh^2 - sinh^2 = 1 and tanh(theta) = x^0/x, and both maps are smooth on their domains because rho > 0 and x - x^0 > 0. Differentiating Phi gives dx^0 = sinh theta d rho + rho cosh theta d theta, dx = cosh theta d rho + rho sinh theta d theta, so -(dx^0)^2 + dx^2 = -rho^2 d theta^2 + d rho^2. The field n is unit future by inspection; a direct computation with the metric gives nabla_{partial_theta} partial_theta = rho partial_rho and hence a = nabla_n n = rho^{-1} partial_rho; the rest slices are the theta-level sets, orthogonal to n because the metric has no theta-rho cross term, with the displayed induced metric independent of theta, so theta_{ab} = 0 and, since the slice is orthogonal to a field whose rest distribution is integrable, omega = 0; the commutator is [rho^{-1}partial_theta, partial_rho] = +(1/rho^2)partial_theta = +(1/rho)n. (c) K is future timelike exactly on the stated U_Omega and is Killing by direct coordinate differentiation. Projecting the symmetric derivative of n=gamma K to its rest space kills the derivative-of-gamma terms (K is parallel to n) and the Killing terms, so theta=0. Put kappa=eta(K,.)=-dx^0+(Omega/c)(x^1 dx^2-x^2 dx^1). Then d kappa=2(Omega/c)dx^1 wedge dx^2 and kappa wedge d kappa=-2(Omega/c)dx^0 wedge dx^1 wedge dx^2, nonzero exactly when Omega!=0. Since n-flat=gamma kappa, n-flat wedge d(n-flat)=gamma^2 kappa wedge d kappa; the stated ambient Frobenius/vorticity result follows, including at the axis by these smooth Cartesian formulas. The Omega=0 limit has the constant unit field. On the ring cylinder, substitute x^0=ct, x^1=Rcos(varphi+Omega t), x^2=Rsin(varphi+Omega t) to obtain the displayed metric and covector. Its one-dimensional kernel is the line field generated by partial_varphi+[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]partial_t, whose integral gives the signed holonomy. A globally defined time-oriented rest-synchronization function would have differential a positive multiple of dt-[Omega R^2/(c^2-Omega^2R^2)]dvarphi. Its integral around a fixed-t ring would have nonzero constant sign for Omega!=0, contradicting exactness of that differential. No local nonintegrability is attributed to the cylinder's one-dimensional rest-line field. (d) Write beta=q_1'/c, beta'=q_1''/c, x^0=ct and n_b=(-gamma,gamma beta,0,0), so partial_0=(1/c)d/dt and partial_1 n_b=0. Differentiation gives partial_0 n_0=-gamma^3 beta beta'/c and partial_0 n_1=gamma^3 beta'/c, using 1+gamma^2 beta^2=gamma^2. Contract with s=(gamma beta,gamma,0,0): s^0[s^0 partial_0 n_0+s^1 partial_0 n_1]=gamma^5 beta beta'(1-beta^2)/c=gamma^3 beta beta'/c=gamma^3 q_1' q_1''/c^3. Projection to the rest space does not change this contraction since s is rest-orthogonal. All transverse expansion components vanish, so it is nonzero exactly under the stated condition, and fixed chart-time separations remain xi_1-xi_2. The material fracture conclusion is excluded. All computations use finite algebra and the declared calculus, with no choice principle.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (i) Flow box. If X is a smooth vector field on Omega and X(p) is nonzero at a point p of Omega, then there is an open neighbourhood U of p in Omega and a chart (u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3): U -> R^4 in which X = partial/partial u^0; the integral curves of X in U are therefore the u^0-coordinate lines up to reparametrization. In particular every observer congruence n on Omega admits a local n-adapted chart, and in such a chart n = partial/partial u^0. (ii) Frobenius criterion. For a smooth nowhere-zero one-form alpha on Omega let D := ker alpha be the hyperplane distribution D_p = {v in V : alpha_p(v) = 0}. Then D is integrable on Omega (through every point there passes a local hypersurface whose tangent space at each of its points is the corresponding D_p) if and only if alpha wedge d alpha = 0 on Omega. (iii) Rest distributions of observer congruences. Let n be an observer congruence on Omega, alpha := n-flat, and let theta, omega be its expansion and vorticity (definition of the congruence kinematics). Then: (a) d alpha = 2 nabla_{[a}n_{b]}, i.e. d alpha(X,Y) = (nabla_X n-flat)(Y) - (nabla_Y n-flat)(X) for smooth vector fields X,Y; (b) for every p and all X,Y with alpha(X) = alpha(Y) = 0 one has d alpha(X,Y) = 2 omega(X,Y); consequently (alpha wedge d alpha)(p) = 0 if and only if omega(p) = 0, and on an open set U contained in Omega the following are equivalent: alpha wedge d alpha = 0 on U, omega = 0 on U, and the rest distribution ker alpha is integrable on U; (c) when the rest distribution is integrable on U, its integral hypersurfaces are orthogonal to n at every point and the restriction of eta to each of them is positive definite, so they are rest slices of the congruence. (iv) Scope. All statements are local on Omega; no global foliation, global synchronization, completeness or product structure is asserted, and no claim is made about variable-rank or non-smooth distributions.
supplier_inspections.strategy: (i) is the published flow-box theorem (thm-flow-box-theorem) applied on the manifold Omega, together with the identification of the integral curves with coordinate lines: in the chart X = partial/partial u^0, so the spatial coordinates are constant along the flow. (ii) is the published codimension-one Frobenius criterion (cor-codimension-one-frobenius-criterion) applied verbatim on the open subset of the smooth manifold A. (iii)(a) is the exterior-derivative identity d alpha(X,Y) = X(alpha(Y)) - Y(alpha(X)) - alpha([X,Y]) for a one-form (def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula) combined with the torsion-freeness nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X = [X,Y] of the flat connection (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space), giving d alpha_{ab} = nabla_a n_b - nabla_b n_a = 2 nabla_{[a}n_{b]}. (iii)(b) for horizontal X,Y the projections in omega_{ab} = h_a{}^c h_b{}^d nabla_{[c}n_{d]} act as the identity on horizontal arguments, so omega(X,Y) = (1/2) d alpha(X,Y); hence alpha wedge d alpha = 0 at a point (which means d alpha vanishes on all pairs of horizontal vectors there) is equivalent to omega = 0 there, and the integrability equivalence on an open set is (ii). (iii)(c) a leaf has tangent space ker alpha_p = n(p)^perp at each of its points, so it is orthogonal to n there, and the restriction of eta to n(p)^perp is positive definite by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c). All steps are local algebra plus the two cited theorems; no choice principle is used.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let c > 0 and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Norm of the four-velocity. Let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration). Then eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^2 for every s in I; equivalently the dimensionless four-velocity u = U/c satisfies eta(u,u) = -1, and U(s) is future timelike. Thus the four-velocity of a worldline lies on the future unit hyperboloid. (b) Orthogonality of the four-acceleration. If x is C^2 at s, then eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0: the four-acceleration has no component along the four-velocity; if in addition A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) is spacelike. (c) Rest space and projection. Let n in V be future unit timelike, eta(n,n) = -1, and put n^perp := {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}. Then n^perp is a 3-dimensional linear subspace of V, the restriction of eta to n^perp is positive definite, and the map h: V -> V, h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n, is linear, idempotent with h o h = h, has image n^perp and kernel span(n), satisfies h(n) = 0 and eta(n,h(v)) = 0 for all v in V, and every v in V has the unique decomposition v = -eta(n,v) n + h(v). Moreover |w| := sqrt(eta(w,w)) defines a norm on n^perp. (d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor. Let n and u be future unit timelike vectors, put gamma := -eta(n,u) and w := c h(u)/gamma. Then gamma >= 1, w lies in n^perp, u = gamma (n + w/c), |w|^2 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and gamma = 1 if and only if u = n. The vector w is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity c u relative to the observer n and gamma is its Lorentz factor. (e) Coordinate form. Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame and let y be a C^1 future timelike worldline whose inertial coordinates are t |-> (c t, r(t)), with coordinate velocity w(t) := r'(t) in R^3 and, when y is C^2, coordinate acceleration a(t) := w'(t). Then |w(t)| < c, the four-velocity is U = gamma_w (c,w) with gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and the four-acceleration is A = gamma_w (d/dt)(gamma_w (c,w)), so that A^0 = gamma_w^4 (w.a)/c and A_vec = gamma_w^2 a + gamma_w^4 (w.a) w/c^2; consequently eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0, with eta(A,A) = 0 if and only if a = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0. For the observer n = e_0 of the chart, clauses (c) and (d) specialize to gamma = gamma_w and w_rel = w. (f) Scope. The statement is a theorem about the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no physical four-velocity. No choice principle is used.
supplier_inspections.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the hard part is (c), which is pure algebra plus one coordinate computation, and the remaining clauses follow from it. (c) Fix an eta-orthonormal basis with e_0 timelike (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis; use an inertial frame of def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Write n = n^0 e_0 + n_s and v = v^0 e_0 + v_s with n_s,v_s in S = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), where eta restricts to the positive definite delta with norm |.| (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame). From eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 one gets (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0. For v with eta(n,v) = -n^0 v^0 + delta(n_s,v_s) = 0 one has v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0, hence eta(v,v) = -(v^0)^2 + |v_s|^2 = |v_s|^2 - delta(n_s,v_s)^2/(n^0)^2 >= |v_s|^2 (1 - |n_s|^2/(n^0)^2) = |v_s|^2/(n^0)^2 >= 0 by the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for delta (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite); equality forces |v_s| = 0 and then v^0 = 0, so v = 0 and the restriction is positive definite. The map v_s |-> v^0 e_0 + v_s with v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0 is a linear bijection S -> n^perp, so n^perp is 3-dimensional. The properties of h are immediate from bilinearity of eta (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-linear-map): eta(n,h(v)) = eta(n,v) + eta(n,v)eta(n,n) = 0, so h(v) lies in n^perp; h(n) = n + eta(n,n)n = 0; h(h(v)) = h(v) + eta(n,h(v))n = h(v); and v = -eta(n,v)n + h(v) is unique because the two summands lie in span(n) and n^perp, which meet only in 0. (a) By def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, U = x'/tau' with tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x',x')), so eta(U,U) = eta(x',x')/(tau')^2 = eta(x',x') c^2/(-eta(x',x')) = -c^2; timelikeness and the future direction of U follow from those of x' and positivity of 1/tau'. (b) eta(U,U) is the constant -c^2 along a C^2 worldline; differentiating componentwise in an eta-orthonormal basis with thm-algebra-of-derivatives gives 0 = (d/ds) eta(U,U) = 2 eta(U,U'), hence eta(U,U') = 0, and dividing by tau' > 0 gives eta(U,A) = 0. If A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) lies in (U(s)/c)^perp, a positive definite space by (c), so eta(A,A) > 0: A(s) is spacelike. (d) By (c), h(u) lies in n^perp and u = gamma n + h(u) with gamma = -eta(n,u). First, gamma > 0: in the inertial frame of (c), future timelikeness of n and u gives n^0 > |n_s| and u^0 > |u_s| (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components), so eta(n,u) = -n^0 u^0 + delta(n_s,u_s) <= -n^0 u^0 + |n_s||u_s| < 0. Second, eta(u,u) = gamma^2 eta(n,n) + eta(h(u),h(u)) = -gamma^2 + |h(u)|^2 = -1, so |h(u)|^2 = gamma^2 - 1 >= 0, giving gamma >= 1; substituting w = c h(u)/gamma gives |w|^2 = c^2 (gamma^2-1)/gamma^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, and solving for gamma gives gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2} and gamma = 1 iff h(u) = 0 iff u = n. (e) In the chart the coordinate path is t |-> (c t, r(t)), so x' = (c,w) and -eta(x',x') = c^2 - |w|^2 > 0 by future timelikeness, giving |w| < c and tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(c^2-|w|^2) = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{1/2} = 1/gamma_w; hence U = x'/tau' = gamma_w (c,w). For C^2 paths, d gamma_w/dt = gamma_w^3 (w.a)/c^2 by thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives (applied to the power -1/2) with the chain rule, and collecting terms in A = gamma_w dU/dt gives the displayed components; expanding eta(A,A) in the diagonal form and using gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2) = 1 gives eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0 with equality iff |a| = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0 agrees with (b). (f) The specialization n = e_0 is the evaluation h(u) = u - u^0 e_0 = (0, w/c gamma_w) and gamma = u^0 = gamma_w, so w_rel = w. No choice principle is used; all arguments are finite-dimensional or one-variable calculus.

unchanged_interfaces_inspected.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: I -> A be a C^2 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U = dx/dtau and four-acceleration A = dU/dtau (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration), so that eta(U,U) = -c^2 and eta(U,A) = 0 pointwise, and A(tau) is spacelike whenever it is nonzero (thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a),(b)). (a) Definition. The proper acceleration of x at the parameter value tau is the real number a(tau) := sqrt(eta(A(tau),A(tau))), the nonnegative square root of def-rational-power. This is well defined for every tau in I: if A(tau) = 0 then eta(A,A) = 0, and if A(tau) is nonzero then it is spacelike and eta(A,A) > 0 (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors); in both cases the argument of the square root is nonnegative, so a(tau) is a nonnegative real number. With the SI coordinate and unit conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, in which x^0 = c t with t in seconds and the spatial coordinates are in metres while eta has the dimensionless matrix diag(-1,1,1,1) in an inertial chart, the components of A carry the unit metre per second squared and eta(A,A) carries the unit (metre per second squared)^2, so a carries the unit metre per second squared. The worldline is uniformly accelerated when a is constant on I. (b) Agreement with the acceleration of a congruence. Let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A and let n: Omega -> V be an observer congruence with acceleration field a_cg := nabla_n n, where nabla is the flat covariant derivative of def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (b)). If x is a flow line of n and U = c n along x, then A = c^2 a_cg along x, and consequently a = c^2 sqrt(eta(a_cg,a_cg)) along x: the proper acceleration is c^2 times the magnitude of the congruence acceleration. In particular the proper acceleration of a congruence worldline is determined by the congruence field alone, and such a worldline is uniformly accelerated exactly when eta(a_cg,a_cg) is constant along it. (c) Reading and scope. This item defines a quantity of the model and fixes its name, its unit and its physical reading. The model reads a(tau) as the magnitude that an ideal accelerometer carried along the worldline would register at tau; this ideal-instrument identification is adopted with the model in the same sense as the framework's ideal-clock reading of proper time and is not derived here. No accelerometer response law, calibration, frequency dependence, force law or interaction is specified or asserted; the definition asserts nothing about which bodies follow which worldlines; no measurement outcome and no statistical, uncertainty or empirical claim is made. No choice principle is used.
unchanged_interfaces_inspected.strategy: Definition with its well-definedness and its unit and congruence clauses justified by the cited suppliers. (a) A is continuous because x is C^2 (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration (b)); eta(A,A) is the sum of products of continuous component functions in any inertial chart (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart, thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions); eta(A,A) >= 0 pointwise by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (b) together with the classification of nonzero spacelike vectors by def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors. Hence sqrt(eta(A,A)) is well defined for every tau as the nonnegative real whose square is eta(A,A) (def-rational-power). Units are read off directly from def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions, which lists the unit metre per second squared for the four-acceleration and the dimensionless matrix diag(-1,1,1,1) for eta in an inertial chart. (b) If U = c n along x with c a constant, then A = dU/dtau = c d(n o x)/dtau; the derivative of the field n along the worldline is the covariant derivative nabla_{dx/dtau} n = nabla_{cn} n = c nabla_n n = c a_cg by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)); hence A = c^2 a_cg and eta(A,A) = c^4 eta(a_cg,a_cg), so a = c^2 sqrt(eta(a_cg,a_cg)) because c > 0. The acceleration a_cg is spacelike or zero by def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (b), so eta(a_cg,a_cg) >= 0. (c) The scope clause records that the accelerometer reading is an ideal-instrument identification of the model and that no apparatus, force or measurement model is asserted; this mirrors the treatment of clock readings in post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and of wave frequencies in def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency. No choice principle is used.
