unchanged_interfaces_inspected.statement: Let c > 0 and alpha > 0, set R := c^2/alpha, and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space with an inertial chart x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3), x^0 = c t (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model, def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Let x: R -> A be the curve x(tau) := x^{-1}(R sinh theta, R cosh theta, 0, 0), where theta := alpha tau/c. (a) Regularity, causal character and parametrization. x is C^infinity, and x'(tau) = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0) is future timelike for every tau (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets), so x is a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline). Since eta(x',x') = -c^2 is constant, the parameter tau is a proper-time parameter of the curve: the proper-time function tau of def-sr-proper-time satisfies tau(b) - tau(a) = b - a for all a < b in R (def-sr-proper-time, lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization), and the four-velocity is U := dx/dtau = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0) with eta(U,U) = -c^2 (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a)). (b) Constant four-acceleration magnitude. The four-acceleration A := dU/dtau = alpha(sinh theta, cosh theta, 0, 0) satisfies eta(A,A) = alpha^2 and eta(U,A) = 0. The chart coordinate velocity is dx^1/dt = c tanh theta, so |dx^1/dt| < c for every tau, and x^1 = R cosh theta > R|sinh theta| = |x^0| for every tau: the worldline lies in the right wedge W := {x^1 > |x^0|} and its speed in the chart tends to c only as tau -> +-infinity. (c) Rindler flow line. Let Phi(theta,rho,y,z) := (rho sinh theta, rho cosh theta, y, z) on R x (0,inf) x R^2 and let n := rho^{-1} partial_theta be the Rindler congruence of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), whose pullback metric is -rho^2 dtheta^2 + drho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 and whose congruence acceleration a_cg := nabla_n n is rho^{-1} partial_rho, with eta(a_cg,a_cg) = rho^{-2} (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space, def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics). Then x is exactly the flow line Phi(., R, 0, 0) reparametrized by theta = alpha tau/c, and along x one has A = c^2 a_cg: the four-acceleration of the worldline is c^2 times the congruence acceleration, and eta(a_cg,a_cg) = 1/R^2 = alpha^2/c^4 on the flow line rho = R. (d) Asymptotic behaviour. Along x one has x^1 - x^0 = R e^{-theta} -> 0 with x^0 -> +infinity as tau -> +infinity, and x^1 + x^0 = R e^{theta} -> 0 with x^0 -> -infinity as tau -> -infinity: the worldline approaches each of the null planes {x^1 = x^0} and {x^1 = -x^0} asymptotically without meeting either, and the chart coordinate speed tends to c at both ends. (e) Scope. This is an exact kinematic computation in the affine model. It uses no force law, no mass, no clock hypothesis and no empirical input; beyond identifying the displayed parameter with the proper time of the curve, only the flow parametrization of the congruence is used. The curve is not asserted to be a geodesic and no statement is made about the forces that would maintain it. No choice principle is used.
unchanged_interfaces_inspected.strategy: Exact computation with the hyperbolic identities and their derivatives. (a) Differentiating the two components of x with the chain rule (thm-chain-rule, def-derivative) and thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives gives x' = c(cosh theta, sinh theta, 0, 0); cosh > 0 makes it future and eta(x',x') = c^2(-cosh^2 + sinh^2) = -c^2 (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). The integrand of def-sr-proper-time is the constant c, so its integral over [a,b] is c(b-a) and tau(b) - tau(a) = b - a; the assertions about the four-velocity then follow from lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization (iv) and thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a). (b) Differentiating U gives A = alpha(sinh theta, cosh theta, 0, 0); eta(A,A) = alpha^2(cosh^2 - sinh^2) = alpha^2 and eta(U,A) = c alpha(-cosh sinh + sinh cosh) = 0 (thm-hyperbolic-identities-and-derivatives); the chart velocity is dx^1/dt = (dx^1/dtau)/(dt/dtau) = c sinh/cosh = c tanh, and cosh > |sinh| gives the wedge and the speed bound. (c) Direct comparison: Phi(theta, R, 0, 0) = (R sinh theta, R cosh theta, 0, 0) = x(tau) with theta = alpha tau/c, and the congruence data are those of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b); the identity A = c^2 a_cg is proved directly on the flow line: since dx/dtau = c n there, d(n o x)/dtau = nabla_{dx/dtau} n = c nabla_n n = c a_cg by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves (def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space (d)), so A = dU/dtau = c d(n o x)/dtau = c^2 a_cg. (d) The identities x^1 -+ x^0 = R(cosh -+ sinh) = R e^{-+theta} and e^{+-theta} -> 0 (thm-exponential-limits-and-range) give the limits; tanh -> +-1 gives the speed statement. (e) Scope only. No choice principle is used: all steps are finite-dimensional algebra and calculus.
